name: Audit Test Report (test-audit-loop)
description: Audits a test_report against the two-criterion contract from OpenSpec change 2026-05-18-test-audit-loop (design.md §A): (1) representativeness — decision record complete, witnesses present, sensitivity evidence varies as predicted; (2) goal alignment — LLM plausibility review of the discrimination_claim against the IAL success criteria. Subscribes to lifecycle:execution:succeeded filtered by output_shapes ∋ 'test_report'. Four tasks: three deterministic checks (check_decision_record_complete, check_witness_presence, check_sensitivity_evidence) plus one LLM resolver (review_alignment_claim, Haiku tier, ≤$0.05). A fifth deterministic task (compose_audit_report) aggregates the four ValidationResult impulses and emits a single test_audit_report via the test_audit_report_write resolver. Audit-specific failure modes are extensions of verifier_negative — failed_evidence carries audit_subtype ∈ {audit_insensitive, audit_noisy, audit_misaligned, audit_record_incomplete} rather than introducing a new top-level failure_mode.type (spec §F). Recursion cap (depth 2) is enforced via the standard composition_chain depth check; lifecycle.parentDepth ≥ 2 triggers a safety_breach short-circuit at compose_audit_report. Witness machinery is reused verbatim from multi-witness-verification (no test-specific witness types).

variables.name: lifecycle
variables.description: Set by the lifecycle dispatcher to the execution:succeeded payload (executionId, templateId, outputShapes, output_impulse_ids, parentDepth, composition_chain). audit-test-report reads parentDepth + composition_chain to enforce the depth-2 recursion cap declared in spec §K and Requirement R5 of specs/test-audit-loop/spec.md.

variables.name: test_report_id
variables.description: Impulse id of the test_report being audited. When invoked via lifecycle subscription, the dispatcher derives this from lifecycle.output_impulse_ids; when invoked directly (workbench, ad-hoc), pass explicitly.

variables.name: test_registration_id
variables.description: Test id of the corresponding test_registration. Derived from test_report.test_registration_id by fetch_test_report when not provided; required for the witness-presence and sensitivity-evidence checks.

variables.name: auditLLMModel
variables.description: Model used by review_alignment_claim. Haiku-tier default keeps the alignment check at ≤$0.05 per audit (design.md §A.2).

tasks.description: Fetch the test_report impulse and the matching test_registration. Both are required inputs for the downstream checks; if either is missing the audit short-circuits with audit_record_incomplete.
tasks.notes: Reads the trace that produced the test_report so the audit has the per-task assertions + tool calls + impulse ids to inspect for decision-record completeness. test_registration is fetched separately by the deterministic checks via discoverByShapesQuery / impulse-resolve when needed — keeping this task light (single trace read) means a missing registration manifests as a caveat at compose_audit_report time, not a fail-fast at fetch time.

tasks.description: Deterministic schema check: every assertion in test_report references a trace event or impulse id. Re-uses the decision_record_completeness schema from multi-witness-verification spec §18-29.
tasks.notes: On fail: emit validation_result with failure_mode = { type: 'verifier_negative', validator_id: 'audit-test-report.check_decision_record_complete', failed_evidence: [{ check_id: 'decision_record_complete', audit_subtype: 'audit_record_incomplete', details: '<missing-field summary>' }] }. The audit_subtype lives inside failed_evidence per spec §F — failure_mode.type stays as verifier_negative, preserving the closed five-type enumeration.

tasks.description: Deterministic check: test_report carries ≥1 witness from test_registration.witness_types (subset of {differential_solve, oracle_label, validator_consensus} per multi-witness-verification spec §58-122). Single-witness reports are tagged passed_with_caveat: 'single_witness' rather than failing.
tasks.notes: Witness types are referenced from multi-witness-verification verbatim — no test-specific witness machinery is introduced (spec §J). A test_report missing all declared witnesses fails with audit_subtype 'audit_record_incomplete'; reports carrying only one declared witness still pass but with caveat 'single_witness' surfaced in the aggregated test_audit_report.caveats[].

tasks.description: Queries sensitivity_evidence impulses for this test_registration over a ≥7-day, ≥3-runs-per-perturbation window. Classifies each perturbation as sensitive / insensitive (observed_delta ≈ 0 when expected_delta ≠ 0) / noisy (observed_delta high-variance across runs).
tasks.notes: Read-only query against the new sensitivity_evidence shape (Phase A). The _post_process block carries the validator parameters the deterministic post-step applies to the returned rows: history below min_runs/min_window emits a caveat 'missing_sensitivity_history' on a passing verdict; insensitive observed deltas emit audit_insensitive; high-variance observed deltas emit audit_noisy. compose_audit_report aggregates these into failed_evidence with the appropriate audit_subtype. The _post_process key sits inside config so the dispatcher passes it through to a validator-style consumer; if a deterministic post-process resolver isn't registered yet, a follow-up LLM task can synthesize the validation_result from the raw evidence rows.

tasks.description: LLM resolver (Haiku tier, ≤$0.05 budget) that reviews test_registration.discrimination_claim for plausibility against the declared IAL success criterion. The LLM verdict is one boolean (plausible: true|false) plus a one-sentence rationale — explicitly NOT a witness (spec §A.2).
tasks.notes: Plausibility-only review — the LLM verdict is NOT a witness for the multi-witness contract. On plausible=false, compose_audit_report aggregates this into failed_evidence with audit_subtype='audit_misaligned' (verifier_negative subtype per spec §F). Budget $0.05 keeps the audit cost-bounded per design.md §A.2.

tasks.description: Aggregate the four ValidationResult impulses into a single test_audit_report and persist via the test_audit_report_write resolver. Enforces the depth-2 recursion cap: when lifecycle.parentDepth ≥ 2 the task emits a safety_breach failure_mode and skips audit-report emission. Carries composition_chain through to the persisted row so meta-audit detection works downstream.

depth_breach_failure_mode.reason: audit chain exceeded depth cap of 2

tasks.notes: The _aggregation block declares (a) which validation_result impulses feed the report; (b) the priority order for picking the dominant audit_subtype when multiple checks fail (record_incomplete first because it invalidates downstream verdicts); (c) the depth-cap guard — when lifecycle.composition_chain length ≥ 2 (parentDepth >= 2 in dispatcher terms) the task emits failure_mode = { type: 'safety_breach', breach_type: 'depth', limit: 2, ancestor_chain: <chain> } and SHORT-CIRCUITS the write, per spec Requirement R5. The recursion cap mirrors create-shape-provider-goal.json's depth guard (compose_goal task); we keep it inline in this task's config rather than as a separate task so a single resolver call decides emit-or-breach. composition_chain on the persisted row enables observability of audit-of-audit chains in the workbench execution browser.

metadata.author: test-audit-loop
metadata.subscriberContract: subscription.shape = 'lifecycle:execution:succeeded' with filter output_shapes_contains = 'test_report'. The dispatcher fires this activity once per test_report emission with the executionId of the producing trace and parentDepth derived from the trace's composition_chain length. Spec Requirement R2: audit MUST begin within 10 minutes of the lifecycle event; harness-side dispatch SLA is enforced by the harness (Phase G), not by this template.
metadata.outputContract: Emits exactly one test_audit_report impulse per dispatch via the test_audit_report_write resolver, or zero impulses when the depth-cap breach short-circuits emission. Caveats array carries 'single_witness' and/or 'missing_sensitivity_history' from the deterministic checks; failed_evidence carries the dominant audit_subtype per the aggregation priority. Spec Requirement R5: depth-cap breaches emit a safety_breach failure_mode trace observable in the standard executionTrace channel, no separate audit-failure surface.
metadata.auditSubtypeContract: Audit-failure subtypes (audit_insensitive, audit_noisy, audit_misaligned, audit_record_incomplete) are extensions of verifier_negative — they live inside failed_evidence[].audit_subtype, NOT as new top-level failure_mode.type values. Spec §F preserves the closed five-type enumeration from validators-and-failure-modes/failure-mode-taxonomy/spec.md.
metadata.witnessReuse: test_registration.witness_types references only multi-witness-verification's three witness types verbatim (differential_solve, oracle_label, validator_consensus). The check_witness_presence task validates that the report carries at least one of those types; no parallel test-witness machinery is introduced (spec §J, Requirement R7).
